title: How We See Things
description: Ray Bot 🤖 powers up a single beam of light. To fight the Shadow Fog you must learn the secret path light takes — and why it always travels in a perfectly straight line.

content.value: The Journey of Light Into Your Eye

We see a non-luminous object in three steps: (1) light from a luminous source falls on the object, (2) the object reflects some of that light, (3) the reflected light enters our eyes. Remove any step and the object vanishes from view.

Light always travels in straight lines. We call these straight paths 'rays'. This is why you cannot see around a corner, and why a torch beam is straight. It is also why shadows form — an opaque object blocks the straight-line path of light, leaving a dark shadow behind it.

TRANSPARENT   → lets almost all light through   (clear glass, water)
TRANSLUCENT   → lets SOME light through, blurry   (frosted glass, tissue)
OPAQUE        → blocks light, makes a shadow      (wood, metal, you!)
You can prove light is straight: line up three cards with a hole in each. You only see the candle when all three holes are in a straight line. Bend one card and the light is blocked!
Key Takeaway: We see objects when reflected light reaches our eyes, and light always travels in straight lines — which is why opaque objects cast shadows.

quiz.question: What is the correct path of light when you see a book?
quiz.explain: Light leaves a source, reflects off the book, and then enters your eye. Your eye does not send out rays to 'find' the book.

quiz.question: Shadows form because light…
options: travels in straight lines and is blocked by opaque objects
quiz.explain: Because light travels straight, an opaque object blocks it and leaves a dark shadow shaped like the object.

quiz.question: Frosted (blurry) glass that lets only some light through is…
quiz.explain: Translucent materials let some light pass but scatter it, so you see only blurry shapes through them.
